prompt: In the process list, which program created `shelf`'s container and then exited?

choices.text: `dockerd`
choices.why: It is still running, and it asks containerd to do the work.

choices.text: `containerd`
choices.why: It is process 428, still running.

choices.text: `runc`
choices.why: Right; the shim stays with the container afterwards.

choices.text: `ctr`
choices.why: `ctr` is a client Ana ran afterwards to look.

prompt: Docker's containers and images live in containerd's namespace called `___`.
Kubernetes stopped going through Docker in 2022. What happened to images built with Docker?

choices.text: They had to be rebuilt with a Kubernetes tool
choices.why: Nothing needed rebuilding.

choices.text: They run only on nodes with Docker installed
choices.why: No Docker is needed on the node.

choices.text: They must be converted to a containerd format first
choices.why: There is one format, the OCI one.

choices.text: They run unchanged, as OCI images
choices.why: Right: containerd reads what Docker writes.

prompt: Order the layers of one `docker run`, from the command down to the process.
Under rootless Podman, `id` inside said `uid=0` and `ps` on the host said `ana`. What does `/proc/self/uid_map` show?
hint: Read the first line: inside, outside, count.

choices.text: UID 0 inside is Ana's 30033 outside
choices.why: Right: root in the container has only Ana's rights on the host.

choices.text: UID 0 inside is UID 0 outside
choices.why: That is Docker's default without remapping.

choices.text: Every UID inside is 65534 outside
choices.why: The map has two ranges, not one.

choices.text: There is no mapping; Podman fakes `id`
choices.why: Nothing is faked; the kernel maps the IDs.

prompt: Why did Podman refuse `golang:1.25` until `unqualified-search-registries` was set?
hint: What would "whichever registry answers first" allow?

choices.text: Podman cannot pull from Docker Hub
choices.why: It pulled from Docker Hub's mirror once told to.

choices.text: It will not guess the registry of a short name
choices.why: Right: a guess could fetch somebody else's image.

choices.text: Tags are not supported in Podman
choices.why: Tags work; the registry was the question.

choices.text: The image did not exist
choices.why: It existed; the name was ambiguous.

prompt: After `podman build`, Ana has `localhost/shelf:1.0.0` in Podman and `shelf:1.0.0` in Docker. How are they related?
hint: Where does each tool keep images?

choices.text: One image with two names
choices.why: Each tool has its own store; nothing is shared here.

choices.text: Podman reads Docker's images directly
choices.why: It does not; it built its own.

choices.text: Two copies in two separate stores
choices.why: Right: same Dockerfile, separate storage.

choices.text: Docker's copy was moved to Podman
choices.why: Docker's is still listed by `docker images`.

prompt: What makes an LXC system container different from the containers in this course?
hint: One program, or a whole system?

choices.text: It runs its own kernel
choices.why: It shares the host's kernel, like any container.

choices.text: It cannot run on Linux
choices.why: It is a Linux technology.

choices.text: It uses OCI images
choices.why: It uses system images of its own.

choices.text: It runs a whole userland with init and services
choices.why: Right: closer to a small VM than to one process.

prompt: Match each tool to its typical use.
A shared server where users must not get root through a container group should run `shelf`. Which fits best?

choices.text: Podman, rootless, run by each user
choices.why: Right: no daemon, and root inside maps to the user outside.

choices.text: Docker, with every user in the `docker` group
choices.why: That gives every user root on the machine.

choices.text: LXC, with `shelf` inside a system container
choices.why: Possible, but it gives up the OCI image the pipeline built.

choices.text: `ctr` as root for everybody
choices.why: That is root for everybody, and a debugging tool besides.
